# The catalog

<!-- Generated by `just gen-catalog-docs` from the TOML under `library/catalog/`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Everything a workspace may install, compiled into the binary from `library/catalog/`. **None of it exists in a
workspace until it is installed.** Ids are bare slugs. An install is transitive, reported, idempotent and never
destructive — see [Agents and teams](../guide/agents-and-teams.md#the-catalog). The three permanent objects — the
General Agent (`library/core/general-agent.toml`), the Workflow Agent (`library/core/workflow-agent.toml`)
and the `general` channel (`library/core/general.toml`) — are not catalog entries: they are ensured at every open.

This page is rendered from the same parse that installs an entry; the contract test in
`crates/bisa-store/tests/it/catalog.rs` holds the sources themselves — references resolve, tags come from the
vocabulary (an addon's tags keep the shape alone), every agent has a fallback model, no agent carries more than six skills, every workflow template
validates with no problems against the catalog's own agents, and every `snake_case` word in the prose is a real MCP
tool.

## Agents (32)

Every prompt ends with its tool wiring: what the role reads before it starts, which tool carries its output,
and when it stops to ask a human. Every agent is `claude-code` with a primary model and a fallback.

## Teams (9)

A team is a named set of members; it cannot contain another team. Installing a team installs its agents and
their skills. **Venture** is the widest entry — 10 candidates every unassigned `agent` step routes across — and the most
expensive to assign; prefer a narrower team when the work belongs to one phase.

| Team | Slug | Purpose | Members |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Design** | `design` | Turns a committed outcome into task flows, screen states and the words in them, so someone can build against it. Happy path, empty, error and loading — before pixels, and before code. | UX Designer, Product Manager, Content Strategist, Document Humanizer |
| **Discovery** | `discovery` | Assigned to a goal that is still a single sentence. Produces a sharpened statement, a read on how the outcome should be judged, and the smallest shape of the work — for the Workflow Agent to draw and the owner to adopt, together with a read on which specialists the work will actually need. It does not build anything. | Product Manager, Business Analyst, Researcher, Facilitator, Critic, General Advisor |
| **Engineering** | `engineering` | Takes committed work items to verified, reviewed change on a branch: the design decision, the implementation — on the web or on a phone —, the review of the diff, the rewrite that makes it read as a person's, and the security read that goes with it. It executes a plan; it does not decide what is worth doing. | Architect, Developer, Mobile Developer, Code Reviewer, Code Humanizer, QA Engineer, Security Engineer |
| **Go-to-Market** | `go-to-market` | Takes something already delivered to demand and revenue: the positioning, the content that carries it, the channels it runs in, and the pipeline that comes out the other end. Every campaign is tied to a number it has to move. | Marketing Manager, Content Strategist, Social Media Manager, Performance Marketer, Sales Lead |
| **Launch** | `launch` | The cross-functional crew for shipping day: the release cut and its rollback, the documentation that has to be true on the day and read as a person wrote it, the announcement, and someone named to be on the hook afterwards. | Release Manager, Technical Writer, Document Humanizer, Communications Lead, Marketing Manager, Site Reliability Engineer |
| **Platform & Operations** | `platform` | Owns how work reaches production and what happens to it there: pipelines, environments, release cuts and incidents. It is the team to assign when the problem is the running system rather than the feature. | DevOps Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer, Security Engineer, Release Manager |
| **Review Board** | `review-board` | The adversarial panel to assign when a decision is expensive or hard to reverse. It attacks the plan, the claim or the result and returns a verdict with the evidence behind it. It never repairs what it finds — that goes back as new work. | Critic, Red Team, Evaluator, QA Engineer |
| **Strategy & Finance** | `strategy` | Answers whether the thing is worth building and what it should cost. Produces the business model, the numbers underneath it, and the assumption that would sink it if it turned out to be wrong — and the legal exposure that comes with the shape it takes. | Business Strategist, Finance Analyst, Business Analyst, Data Analyst, Legal Advisor |
| **Venture** | `venture` | Every phase staffed at once, from the business case to the first customer, so one goal can go end to end with the fewest handoffs and someone sequencing the ones that remain. This is the widest team here and therefore the most expensive one to assign — prefer a narrower team when the work belongs to a single phase. | Product Manager, Project Manager, Business Strategist, Architect, Developer, QA Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Marketing Manager, Sales Lead, Finance Analyst |

## Channels (8)

A standing channel with a roster. Installing one installs its roster. `general` is not here — it is permanent
and its roster policy is *everyone*.

| Channel | Topic | Roster |
|---|---|---|
| `business` | The model, pricing, budget, the metrics that say whether any of it is working, and the legal exposure the shape of it carries. Figures posted here are worth marking as measured or assumed. | Business Strategist, Finance Analyst, Data Analyst, Legal Advisor |
| `delivery` | What is blocked, what slipped, what ships when, and who is told. The room for the schedule and the handoffs between roles, as opposed to what is broken right now (operations) or what is worth building at all (product). | Project Manager, Release Manager, Technical Writer, Document Humanizer, Communications Lead |
| `engineering` | Design decisions, implementation questions, review of a diff, and what broke in the build. Incidents in production belong in operations. | Architect, Developer, Mobile Developer, Code Reviewer, Code Humanizer, QA Engineer, Security Engineer |
| `go-to-market` | Positioning, content, campaigns and pipeline — how the thing is described to people who do not work on it, and what that brings in. | Marketing Manager, Content Strategist, Social Media Manager, Performance Marketer, Sales Lead |
| `ideas` | Half-formed thoughts, before any of them is worth a goal. The ones that survive the room become goals; nothing here is a commitment. | Facilitator, Critic, Researcher, Business Strategist, General Advisor |
| `operations` | Incidents, deploys, health checks, and the state of anything currently running. The room to open when something is broken now rather than wrong by design. | Site Reliability Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Release Manager, Security Engineer |
| `product` | Scope, acceptance criteria, priorities, and what a user is actually trying to do. Where a request gets argued down to what it really asks for. | Product Manager, Business Analyst, UX Designer |
| `review` | Verdicts and the evidence under them: the rubric before the scoring, the attack on a plan, the diff that does not hold, the criterion that failed. Nothing is repaired here — a finding leaves as new work. | Critic, Red Team, Evaluator, QA Engineer, Code Reviewer, Code Humanizer |

## Workflows (13)

A workflow template is a whole workflow — inputs and steps — that a goal runs, or that the workspace runs.
Installing one installs the catalog agents its `agent` steps name and the templates its `spawn` steps start. People
and projects are never in a template: they arrive as inputs when the run starts. The shape an `agent` step yields
is its `output_schema`, shown to the session with every prompt; a later step reads a required field of it, from a step sure to have run before it.
Every template begins at a `start` step a person runs by hand; 4 begin on an event too — a schedule, a
call, a check that starts failing, a run that ended — and hear it once the workflow is turned On, or a goal that
runs it listens. A template installs Off. The *Starts on* column is each start's event, in definition order; the
*Shape* column is the steps in definition order; `bisa workflow show <slug> --json` prints a template in full.
Guides: [Workflows](../guide/workflows.md), [Events and gateways](../guide/events.md).

## Connectors (15)

A connector is a declarative definition of one outside platform's API — its hosts, its auth scheme, a handful
of its most useful operations — that a `connector` step calls. Nothing here holds a credential: an **account** is
added on the machine that has one (Settings › Capabilities › Connectors, or `bisa connector account add`), its secrets live in
the keystore, and the definition names the account only at run time. An operation marked *writes* changes something
on the platform; a workflow puts an `approval` step before it. Guide: [Connectors](../guide/connectors.md).

## Addons (13)

An addon is a folder of HTML, CSS and JavaScript that floats over the desktop in a window its developer shaped, runs
behind three walls and reaches the platform only through what the person granted ([18 — Addons](../architecture/18-addons.md)).
These ship in the binary from `library/addons/` and install on demand from Settings › Library › Addons, granted what they
declare; a folder of your own imports there with nothing granted until you say so. Guide: [Addons](../guide/addons.md).

| Addon | Slug | For | Version | Window | Permissions | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Calculator** | `calculator` | Four functions, a backspace and a keyboard, for the arithmetic between two thoughts — left to right, as typed. | 0.2.0 | 220×300 | — | `tool` |
| **Clock** | `clock` | The time on one face — analog with a sweeping second hand, or digital — 12 or 24 hours, the date if you like; the settings behind a gear. | 0.2.0 | 200×200 | `storage` | `time` |
| **CPU** | `cpu` | The machine's processor load as a sparkline, at the footer's cadence. | 0.2.0 | 160×64 | `system_load` | `load` `system` |
| **Disk** | `disk` | The volume the platform's data lives on: used against total, and what the workspace itself weighs. | 0.2.0 | 160×64 | `system_load` | `load` `system` |
| **GPU** | `gpu` | The accelerator's load as a sparkline, where the machine reports one. | 0.2.0 | 160×64 | `system_load` | `load` `system` |
| **Memory** | `memory` | Memory in use against what the machine has, as a bar and a number. | 0.2.0 | 160×64 | `system_load` | `load` `system` |
| **Needs you** | `needs-you` | How many things wait on you, are under review, or are running — a click goes to them. | 0.2.0 | 200×88 | `workspace_summary`, `navigate` | `attention` `workspace` |
| **Pomodoro** | `pomodoro` | Twenty-five minutes on, five off, a ring that empties and a notice at each turn; the lengths are yours to set. | 0.2.0 | 200×150 | `notify`, `storage` | `focus` `time` |
| **Sticky note** | `sticky-note` | As many notes as you like on one pad — a dot per note, six papers, bold, italic, underline and lists — each remembered as you type. | 0.2.0 | 220×180 | `storage`, `clipboard_write` | `notes` `tool` |
| **Stopwatch** | `stopwatch` | Start, lap, reset — time as it passes, with every lap numbered. | 0.2.0 | 200×110 | — | `time` `tool` |
| **Tic-tac-toe** | `tic-tac-toe` | You against the machine — easy or unbeatable — or two players at one board, with a tally per mode; a break that fits in a corner. | 0.2.0 | 220×270 | `storage` | `break` `game` |

## Pets (9)

A pet is an animated companion that floats over the desktop and shows what the agents are doing — running, waiting on you,
done. These nine ship inside the platform, drawn against the sheet's nine states with each pet's own pace; nothing installs them
and nothing removes them. **Moonrice** is the one shown when the pet is turned on and none was chosen. A pack of your own in
Codex's format imports under Settings › You › Pet. Guide: [The pet](../guide/the-desktop.md#the-pet).

| Pet | Id | Tagline | Archetype | Mood |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bracket** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.bracket` | Grows on what you delete. | shroom | happy |
| **Buffer** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.buffer` | Steady state. | snail | sleepy |
| **Fathom** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.fathom` | Reads all the way down. | squid | curious |
| **Jolt** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.jolt` | It's 3am and Jolt has ideas. | gremlin | wired |
| **Kernel** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.kernel` | Has chosen your keyboard. The matter is closed. | cat | smug |
| **Loop** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.loop` | Runs it again. | mech | neutral |
| **Lumen** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.lumen` | Ships by lamplight. | moth | dreamy |
| **Moonrice** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.moonrice` | Brought you something warm. | ghost | serene |
| **Nocturn** | `bisa-pets.midnight-shipping.nocturn` | Keeps watch while you keep going. | owl | stoic |

## The tag vocabulary

Every tag in this catalog is one of these — an addon's keep the shape alone — and the contract test refuses any other. A tag a person writes is free-form: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

```
business · code · content · data · delivery · design · discovery · engineering
legal · management · marketing · mobile · ops · planning · product · quality
research · review · sales · security · thinking · web · writing
```
